motivation: A stable high-occupancy bundle can remain internally coherent while losing continuity with the capability-bearing reference subspace. Occupancy measures coherence, not identity.

reference_rule.synthetic_sweeps: smallest strictly positive registered perturbation level
reference_rule.real_model: preregistered calibration prompt/run family chosen without outcomes
reference_rule.zero_noise: legacy RNG compatibility point; prohibited as the paired positive-noise reference

target_blind_features.worst_direction_retention: minimum squared singular value of U_ref^T U_t, with zero padding under rank loss
target_blind_features.maximum_principal_angle_degrees: largest principal angle, with 90 degrees assigned to missing reference dimensions

soft_lineage_operator: A_t = P_t P_ref P_t, a positive-semidefinite contraction used descriptively beside the hard consensus projector
rl_feature: x^T A_t x / ||x||^2; compare against hard bundle energy and the full frozen nuisance/Jacobian baseline under the same grouped splits
edit_feature: coordinates after target-blind orthogonal Procrustes alignment of U_t to U_ref; proposals remain normalized, hashed, and unapplied

sealing.timing: all lineage features and reference assignments are serialized and hashed before outcome join

evaluation.primary_question: Does lineage add grouped-held-out predictive value beyond occupancy, rank, eigengap, edit norm, nuisance covariates, and Jacobian visibility?
evaluation.status_rule: descriptive until replicated real-model outcomes; no gate may be introduced from the same outcomes used to tune it

stop_conditions: reference assignment cannot be made without outcomes
operator hashes or exact edit-space layouts differ
lineage feature table is not sealed before outcome join
grouped evaluation lacks independent run replicates
claim_boundary: A positive result would show that target-blind subspace continuity adds predictive information beyond coherence. It would not establish semantic identity, safe self-improvement, compactification, or RSI.
